Speech and Language Therapy
We’re happy to share information for parents and carers about speech, language and occupation support at Lansdowne School.
This is an important part of the support that we are able to offer to pupils. We have a dedicated team of professional who work with the students to hep improve their communication skills.
All students throughout the school are encouraged to use the Zones of Regulation. This is a colour coded scheme to help express emotions. You can learn more about this over here.
Lego Club is an evidence-based approach designed to support and develop students’ social communication skills. These skills include turn-taking, listening and following directions, giving instructions, problem solving and joint attention.
You can find out more over here.
Blank’s levels of questioning is a questioning framework which aims to develop student’s verbal reasoning, comprehension, inferencing, predicting and problem-solving skills.
We have more details to share over here.

pageCache.text:
Colourscape Visit Lansdowne
Colourscape Workshop Visited Lansdowne for the week.
Last week, all pupils had the wonderful opportunity to experience a workshop with ColourScape, where they experimented with sound, light and colour to create their own original musical compositions and paint pouring patterns. The photos below give a glimpse of the extraordinary results and the fun the pupils had throughout the process.
All of the pupils had the opportunity to take part in the ColourScape light and sound workshops. In the sessions, the pupils were able to make their own music using instruments that work through laser beams and touch pads. The pupils worked in their groups to produce and perform their own compositions which included the instruments, their vocals and the colourful light display.
Pupils at Lansdowne School had an wonderful week with the visiting ColourScape Experience, taking over our art rooms to deliver fascinating and creative art activities. Pupils enjoyed making paint pouring with a real artist, creating surprising, organic and dreamy colourful patterns, with the added mystery of not knowing what patterns and colour blends they would get as they poured their paint combinations. In another art room, pupils had the opportunity to create sound landscapes, using sound, lights and colours to project vibrant and joyful silhouettes all around each other. It was really exciting to have ColourScape in school, and transform our art rooms and to meet real life artists. Thank you ColourScape! —Ms Mendonςa

Useful Careers Resources for Pupils and Parents
The National Careers Service provides information, advice and guidance to help students make decisions on learning, training and work opportunities. The service offers confidential and impartial advice and is supported by qualified careers advisers. You can chat with an adviser using webchat (8am to 10pm, 7days a week). Or you can call 0800 100 900 to speak to an adviser (8am to 10pm, 7 days a week). Calls are free from landlines and most mobile numbers.
The National Apprenticeship Service website offers guidance on how to apply for an apprenticeship as well as listing current local apprenticeship opportunities. More information on apprenticeships can be found at amazingapprenticeships.com.
CareersBox is a free online library of careers related videos, news and information.
Careers Advice for Parents aims to give parents an easy-to-read overview of all the essential facts on finding jobs and apprenticeships or choosing further and higher education courses which could make a real difference to their child’s future career prospects.
The weekly CfBT LMI Bulletin provides up to date information on regional developments and vacancies . Parental Guidance offers advice and information on all aspects of the process of career choice for young people aged 13 to 25.

Federation Attendance and Punctuality
Lansdowne Turney Federation Attendance and Punctuality
You can only allow your child to miss school if either:
It is important that all pupil absence is reported to the school office on the first morning of absence. The school office opens at 7.00am.
It is a legal requirement that all parents and carers report when their child is absent from school, whatever the reason, giving details of when and how long their child is likely to be absent.
Unauthorised absences will be investigated by the school and where absences cause concern, they will be referred to Educational Welfare Services.
You have to get permission from the head teacher if you want to take your child out of school during term time.
You can only do this if:
It’s up to the head teacher how many days your child can be away from school if leave is granted. If you do really need to take your child out of school during term time you must make it very clear in your request how the circumstances are exceptional.
